transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-11
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Sophie Alvarez (Brightline Procurement), Markus Ibsen (Brightline Legal), Ravi Patel (Brightline Security)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be partial):
Quick escalation of MSA/DPA points, clarify SLA requirements and pricing exceptions pathway. Discussed private deployment vs hosted data residency, KMS integration, and procurement approval flow. Agreed to exchange redlines and schedule a finance+proc meeting.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA exceptions, SLA targets (p95 latency, monthly uptime), pricing exceptions & approvals, VPC/private deployment options, KMS/HSM, pilot scope and timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: All right hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i have Devon with me from engineering, how are you folks?
[00:10] Sophie: Hey thanks Maya, doing well, appreciate you setting this up. We wanted to move the MSA along and also get clarity on the DPA — our counsel's got a few notes.
[00:18] Markus: Yes, hi — Markus here. We sent high-level redlines yesterday but wanted to walk through a couple of specific items, like data retention, and liability caps.
[00:26] Devon: Hi Markus, hi Sophie, quick note: I'll try to keep the tech bits brief but want to call out where hosting affects legal concerns — e.g., private deployment changes the scope of our obligations.
[00:34] Sophie: Great. If it's ok we'll start with procurement timeline, then jump to the technical constraints and legal items.
[00:41] Maya: Sounds good. Sophie, what's your needed timeline for onboarding?
[00:45] Sophie: We're aiming for a go/no-go to vendor selection by end of month. Procurement needs pricing approvals and MSA signoff; finance wants clarity on overage billing and price floors. We may need a pricing exception if the committed capacity is under X GPUs.
[00:58] Maya: Understood. We can map pricing pathways — there's the standard hosted pricing and then reserved/ Dedicated pricing and private deployment licensing. We can put together a clear path for exceptions.
[01:10] Markus: On the MSA, the main asks: more explicit audit rights, data residency guarantees, stronger indemnity language for PHI. We're in healthcare so PHI concerns are front and center.
[01:22] Devon: Right, technically we support VPC-only private instances and on-prem packages. For PHI we'll recommend Private with customer-managed KMS/HSM, audit logs, and put controls in place — though some of those require enterprise licensing.
[01:35] Sophie: Can you say more about KMS integration? Our security team wants proof we can do a customer-managed key.
[01:40] Devon: Sure. Redwood supports bring-your-own-key patterns — we can integrate with most cloud KMS providers, and we offer an HSM-backed option for Private deployments. There's some work for key rotation and ledgering to align with your audit policies. I'll follow up with a short tech memo.
[01:57] Markus: Do you have SOC2/ISO attestations? Our legal wants those attachments with the DPA.
[02:02] Maya: Yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs; I'll share the cert bundle and the security whitepaper link after the call.
[02:10] Sophie: Excellent. On the DPA, Markus flagged a 3rd party subprocessors list — we need visibility and the ability to object to certain sub processors.
[02:19] Devon: We can provide a current subprocessor list; policy is to notify customers about changes and there's a process for high-risk objections, though typically that ties into the Private/ Dedicated options.
[02:29] [02:30] Sophie: Okay. For SLA specifics, our SRE wants p95 inference latency under 500ms for short prompt workloads and 99.9% monthly availability. Is that feasible?
[02:40] Maya: For hosted, we have published performance profiles; 500ms p95 is achievable with certain model classes and batching configs, but at scale you hit tradeoffs. With Dedicated we can give tighter SLOs and carve a commitment for that 99.9% availability.
[02:55] Devon: One nuance: latency SLOs depend on model choice, sequence length, and KV cache hit rates. We can reserve capacity to meet the SLOs but if you want PHI controls and private routing that increases cost.
[03:10] Markus: Cost is ok if it's justified. The procurement question is how to document pricing exceptions and approvals — do we need a separate MSA exhibit or a PO workflow?
[03:20] Maya: We typically handle pricing commitments via an order form / exhibit tied to the MSA. For exceptions, we can add an Appendix that outlines the approved exception and approval matrix. We'll supply template language.
[03:30] Sophie: Good. Also finance asked: how do overage rates work with usage spikes from seasonal surges?
[03:36] Maya: Overage is at the committed-tier rate or an established surge rate; for Dedicated we can do burst capacity at a negotiated multiplier. We'll include example calculations in the pricing sheet.
[03:47] [03:50] Ravi: Quick security note — we need clarity on logs retention and redaction for PHI. Can Redwood redact logs or do we need to route logs to our SIEM?
[03:58] Devon: The platform can redact at ingestion for certain fields but for full auditability we recommend forwarding logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding; for Private deployments we can also configure log sinks into your VPC.
[04:14] Sophie: That's helpful. Markus, any legal non-starters?
[04:18] Markus: The liability cap currently tied to fees is concerning for PHI; we want higher cap or carveouts for data breach. Also need stronger breach notifications and SLA credits spelled out.
[04:28] Maya: We can propose language for carveouts and an escalation playbook. We usually see compromise with a higher cap for specific PHI incidents and clear notification timelines (e.g., 72 hours).
[04:40] Markus: 72 hours is workable if we have a remediation plan and cooperation obligations.
[04:46] [04:50] Sophie: On subprocessors we will send a list of vendors we cannot allow and ask you to confirm compatibility.
[04:56] Devon: OK we'll do a subprocessors matrix and flag any that are a concern.
[05:02] Maya: I'll upload an annotated MSA with our baseline redlines and call out the high-priority items.
[05:07] Sophie: Great. I also want a clear list of stakeholders for approvals; procurement typically needs CPO and finance signoff.
[05:14] Maya: Good, we'll include a one-pager that maps approvals to names/roles.
[05:18] [05:20] Markus: One more legal point — IP indemnity around model outputs. We need assurance on third-party content and how Redwood handles claims.
[05:27] Devon: Model output IP is tricky. We provide indemnity for code/exact model artifacts in specified cases, but we recommend a usage policy and a training data disclosure in the DPA/appendix. We'll write conservative language to limit exposure.
[05:42] Sophie: Ok. For procurement gating, what's your normal internal time for MSA negotiation once redlines are exchanged?
[05:48] Maya: For straightforward redlines, 1-2 weeks. For deeper legal and security escalations that involve our enterprise team, 3-6 weeks typically.
[05:57] Sophie: Noted.
[06:00] [06:05] Maya: Pricing pathway — Devon, do you want to explain Dedicated vs Private cost drivers?
[06:09] Devon: Sure. Hosted (pay-as-you-go) has lowest startup friction but variable costs. Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity with a monthly commit — better unit economics and predictable latency. Private includes licensing and network integration costs; usually higher fixed fee but required for strict residency/PHI controls. Quantization and batching can reduce per-token cost.
[06:30] Sophie: If we commit to a pilot (3 months) with a small dedicated pool, can we get a temp price lock?
[06:36] Maya: Yes we can provision a pilot PO with locked pricing for the pilot duration and then renegotiate at scale.
[06:41] [06:45] Markus: For SLAs during pilot, can you offer a reduced commitment but with reporting that meets our compliance needs?
[06:52] Devon: We can provide monitoring access and weekly reports; SLA credits usually require a baseline commit, but we can put in a tailored reporting annex for pilot.
[07:02] Sophie: Good. Next up — procurement needs the DPA specifics. Do you accept our standard DPA or want to use Redwood's?
[07:10] Maya: We prefer Redwood's DPA for speed, but we will map your changes. If you send your redline we'll do a side-by-side and call out any hard stops.
[07:20] Markus: We'll send redlines; expectation is to have an initial response within 3 business days. Is that ok?
[07:25] Maya: Yes that aligns with our SLA.
[07:28] [07:30] Sophie: On the data residency front, we need EU-only processing for a subset of workloads. Can you route requests to a region and guarantee no egress?
[07:38] Devon: Yes for Hosted we can enforce region routing; for full guarantee we recommend Private or Dedicated located in EU region with contractual egress restrictions. There are network egress audits we can provide.
[07:50] Sophie: Excellent.
[07:53] Maya: Quick note — I'll also attach our KMS/HSM spec and an architecture diagram to the shared folder. The link will be in the follow-up email.
[07:59] [08:00] Ravi: A practical ask: can you share a short checklist of the security controls we can evaluate quickly? We have a 1-week window for the initial security review.
[08:07] Devon: Yes I'll produce a 1-2 page checklist: KMS support, encryption-at-rest/in-transit, logging, RBAC/SSO, network isolation, and audit trails.
[08:16] Sophie: Please include expected artifact delivery dates in that checklist.
[08:19] Devon: Will do.
[08:21] [08:30] Maya: Let's talk about procurement approvals — Sophie, who signs off on pricing exceptions?
[08:34] Sophie: Typically CPO for vendor selection and CFO/finance for commercial exceptions. I'll confirm exact names and share.
[08:40] Maya: Great. We want to avoid surprises in pricing committee; we'll prepare a one-page economics summary and an example invoice.
[08:48] Markus: Back to liability — if we accept higher cap for PHI incidents, we need a defined mitigation plan and obligations.
[08:56] Maya: Understood. We can attach an incident response appendix to commit to cooperation, timely notifications, and specific remediation steps.
[09:04] [09:10] Sophie: Two quick procedural things: 1) where do you want us to upload redlines? 2) Do you require NDA before sharing architecture?
[09:18] Maya: Upload redlines to the shared drive link that I'll send; NDA — we can share the general architecture now, but for deeper docs we can sign a mutual NDA; I think you already raised one earlier?
[09:28] Sophie: We have a standing NDA but I'll double-check and confirm.
[09:32] Devon: Also small detail — if you want logs routed to your SIEM we'll need a network peering window and some firewall rules; we can draft that out.
[09:41] [09:45] Maya: Any other blockers?
[09:47] Markus: Not blockers, just wanting timelines. If we get your memos and the annotated MSA this week, legal can turn around initial review within 5 business days.
[09:58] Maya: Perfect. We'll aim for that.
[10:01] [10:05] Sophie: On pricing exceptions: if we put a pilot PO for 3 months with a small committed GPU count, we will need a clause that allows us to convert to enterprise commit or terminate with 30 days.
[10:15] Maya: That's reasonable, we can include pilot termination terms and conversion steps.
[10:20] Devon: From operations side, we'll need a kickoff call with your platform team to map network and monitoring. Recommend a 1-hour technical onboarding session after paperwork.
[10:31] Sophie: Ok plan that.
[10:34] [10:40] Maya: Quick recap before we close — action items and owners: I'll upload the annotated MSA and certs; Devon will produce the security checklist and Private deployment memo; Sophie will circulate procurement approvers and vendor restrictions; Markus will send DPA redlines.
[10:54] Sophie: Yep. Also ask that you include examples of SLA credit calculations in the appendix.
[11:00] Maya: Will do.
[11:03] [11:10] Markus: Thanks everyone, this was productive.
[11:12] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with the shared link and a proposed timeline.
[11:16] Sophie: Thanks, bye.
[11:18] Devon: Bye.

End of transcript.
